caption:
Women's share of India Inc leadership has slipped from 20% to 16.7%, according to reporting published by Business Today on 10 September 2026. Verify the underlying figures before you quote them. But note what the number does: it takes a private grievance "I said it first, he said it second, the room heard him" and makes it a structural fact you can put on a slide.

That changes the conversation. A feeling can be dismissed. A trend line cannot.

It does not change what happens in the room at 9:40 on a Tuesday. That is still bearing, tone, and the discipline to hold a silence until the room comes to you. In 35 years of command, Colonel Suhag saw the same truth repeatedly: authority is not granted by the table. It is carried in.

Use the data to argue for the system. Use the method to hold your ground while the system catches up.
alt_text: A plain dark slide with large text reading "20% to 16.7%" and smaller text below noting the drop in women's share of India Inc leadership, with the Lumina Presence wordmark in the lower corner.

topic.title: Women in India Inc leadership slipping from 20% to 16.7%
topic.angle: A large share of the brand's 'qualified but consistently overlooked' audience is women in Indian management whose daily experience of being talked over now has an external number attached, turning a private grievance into a structural, discussable fact.
topic.why_now: Business Today published the 20% to 16.7% framing on 10 September 2026 and it's still circulating, sitting just ahead of the Q3 close and the leadership-appointment commentary cycle — though the underlying figures need one click of verification before publishing.

rationale: A stark numbers-only visual lets the statistic carry the weight without decoration, matching the brand's plainspoken, no-nonsense register.
